name: Rasterization pipeline
definition: Turning scene geometry into pixels, including the render graph and pass structure.
interop_reason: How a system turns geometry into pixels never leaves that system, so two runtimes can draw the same scene by different means and nothing crosses.

name: Graphics interface binding
definition: Which low-level graphics interface the renderer targets.
interop_reason: The graphics interface a runtime targets is a build choice inside one system, and an arriving asset cannot tell the difference.

name: Material model
definition: How surface appearance is described and evaluated at render time.
interop_reason: An asset that arrives against a different surface model still loads, but the further apart the two models are the more the look drifts.

name: Lighting and global illumination
definition: Direct and indirect light, shadows, probes, baked or real time.
interop_reason: A moved scene whose lights are read differently is lit wrong rather than lost.

name: Post-processing
definition: Effects applied after the main render pass.
interop_reason: Effects applied after the main pass are the receiving system's taste and carry nothing across.

name: Level of detail and streaming order
definition: Choosing what detail to show and what to send first. An interoperability question once geometry is streamed.
interop_reason: Without an agreed order for what to send first, a large scene still arrives, it just pops and stalls on the way in.

name: Gaussian splatting and radiance fields
definition: Rendering captured scenes represented as splats or radiance fields rather than meshes.
interop_reason: Only content captured as splats is affected: a system that cannot draw them shows nothing of it, while mesh content is untouched.

name: Volumetric and point cloud
definition: Rendering point clouds, voxels and volumetric video.
interop_reason: The same holds for point clouds and volumetric video, which travel in forms few systems read.

name: Text rendering
definition: Legible text in three dimensions, including fonts and layout.
interop_reason: Labels, signs and name tags lose their font and layout when the two systems disagree, so the text degrades while the rest of the asset is fine.

name: Camera and viewpoint model
definition: How viewpoints are defined, bound and moved between.
interop_reason: Authored viewpoints are part of a scene, and losing them costs the arrival shot, not the scene.

name: Scene graph model
definition: The tree or graph of objects and their relationships.
interop_reason: If the receiving system cannot rebuild the same tree, parenting and transforms collapse and the asset does not assemble at all.

name: Transforms and coordinate convention
definition: Handedness, axis order, and how transforms compose.
interop_reason: A disagreement about handedness or axis order puts every object in the wrong place or mirrored, which is the classic hand fix.

name: Asset container format
definition: The file that carries a model or scene between tools and runtimes.
interop_reason: The file is the boundary: if the second system cannot open it, nothing else on this list matters.

name: Geometry encoding
definition: How meshes are encoded and compressed.
interop_reason: A mesh encoded in a way the receiver cannot decode is not a mesh, and the compression choice is where this usually breaks.

name: Texture encoding
definition: Image formats and compression for the target device.
interop_reason: Device-specific texture compression is the common failure: the model arrives untextured and someone must re-export it.

name: Material exchange
definition: Carrying material definitions between different renderers without loss.
interop_reason: Carrying materials without loss is what "renders in another system" means, and only two subjects reach this row natively today.

name: Animation encoding
definition: How keyframes and animation clips are stored and replayed.
interop_reason: A clip that cannot be read leaves the object still, and an avatar that cannot move is not an avatar.

name: Skeleton and rig definition
definition: Bone hierarchy and binding, so a body moves correctly elsewhere.
interop_reason: The bone hierarchy is what makes a body move correctly elsewhere; without an agreed one, motion has nothing to bind to.

name: Morph targets and blend shapes
definition: Shape deformation used for faces and detail.
interop_reason: Blend shapes carry facial detail, so losing them freezes a face rather than stopping the transfer.

name: Instancing
definition: Repeating an object many times cheaply.
interop_reason: A scene without agreed instancing still loads, it just costs far more memory and frames.

name: Scene composition and overrides
definition: Layering, referencing and overriding parts of a scene from several sources.
interop_reason: Layered references are a working convenience, and flattening on export is the fallback that keeps the asset moving.

name: Units and scale
definition: Real-world scale agreement so imported content is the right size.
interop_reason: A metre read as a centimetre makes the asset useless on arrival, and rescaling by hand is the fix the use case forbids.

name: Rights and licence metadata
definition: What a recipient is permitted to do with an asset, carried with the asset.
interop_reason: An item that arrives with no readable terms cannot be lawfully worn, shown or sold, so the move fails at the rights boundary even when every byte arrives.

name: Provenance and authorship
definition: Signed record of who made an asset and how.
interop_reason: A signed record of who made an asset lets a receiver trust it; without one the asset still works but nobody can check its history.

name: Avatar body format
definition: The portable description of an avatar's mesh and appearance.
interop_reason: The portable description of the body is the artefact this use case moves; with no agreement the person arrives as nothing.

name: Avatar skeleton standard
definition: An agreed bone naming and structure so animation transfers.
interop_reason: Agreed bone names are what let animation authored anywhere play on the arriving body.

name: Facial expression standard
definition: Named expressions and visemes that survive a move between worlds.
interop_reason: The use case names expressions, and named shapes the destination does not know leave a blank face.

name: Animation retargeting
definition: Playing animation authored for one body on another.
interop_reason: Retargeting is the repair when skeletons differ, so its absence costs motion quality rather than the visit.

name: Attachments and wearables
definition: Items worn or carried, with attachment points that survive transfer.
interop_reason: Equipped items are named in the use case, and attachment points that do not survive leave items on the floor or on the wrong bone.

name: Avatar level of detail
definition: Reduced avatar representations for crowds and weak devices.
interop_reason: Reduced forms matter for crowds and weak devices, and their absence costs frames, not presence.

name: Avatar to identity binding
definition: Tying an avatar to a verifiable identity or credential.
interop_reason: Without a way to bind an avatar to a verifiable identity, the person who arrives cannot be shown to be the person who left.

name: Rigid bodies
definition: Mass, velocity and the bodies that move by rule.
interop_reason: Mass and velocity carried across make a moved object behave nearly the same; their absence changes the behaviour without stopping it.

name: Collision shapes
definition: The shapes used for contact tests, separate from visible geometry.
interop_reason: Collision shapes travel separately from visible geometry, and losing them means objects pass through each other until the destination builds its own.

name: Joints and constraints
definition: Hinges, sliders and other links between bodies.
interop_reason: Hinges and sliders that do not survive turn an assembly into loose parts, which is a loss of behaviour rather than of the asset.

name: Physics materials
definition: Friction, restitution and surface response.
interop_reason: Friction and restitution numbers mean different things to different solvers, so agreeing on them buys little and each world may keep its own feel.

name: Deterministic simulation
definition: Same inputs producing the same outcome on different machines.
interop_reason: Two engines producing the same trajectory would let one object be simulated in two places at once, and nothing does that today.

name: Soft bodies and cloth
definition: Deformable simulation.
interop_reason: Cloth and hair are the visible part, so a moved avatar arrives stiff rather than absent.

name: Trigger volumes
definition: Regions that fire events when entered.
interop_reason: Regions that fire events are part of how content behaves, and their loss makes the content inert rather than unreadable.

name: Positioned audio sources
definition: Sound placed in the scene with distance and direction.
interop_reason: Positioned sounds are authored into a scene, and losing them leaves a silent room.

name: Spatialization model
definition: How direction is rendered to the ears, by head-related transfer or ambisonics.
interop_reason: How direction is turned into sound at the ears is the receiving system's method, like a rendering method.

name: Room acoustics and reverb
definition: How a space colours sound.
interop_reason: A space's acoustic description is authored with it, and without agreement the room sounds wrong rather than silent.

name: Occlusion and obstruction
definition: Sound blocked or muffled by geometry.
interop_reason: The receiving runtime works this out from its own geometry, frame by frame.

name: Audio streaming
definition: Delivering audio over the network at scale.
interop_reason: A visitor can be given audio by other means, so disagreement costs quality and scale.

name: Voice transport
definition: Carrying live voice between participants.
interop_reason: A visitor who cannot be heard is diminished but still present, and text remains a fallback.

name: State replication
definition: Which state is shared, how often, and in what form.
interop_reason: A client or agent that cannot read the destination's state stream arrives blind, which ends both use cases on the spot.

name: Authority and ownership
definition: Who decides the truth for a given object.
interop_reason: Disagreement about who owns an arriving object shows up as rubber-banding and contested edits rather than as a failed arrival.

name: Interest management
definition: Sending each client only what it needs.
interop_reason: Without agreement the destination sends everything or too little, which costs scale.

name: Prediction and reconciliation
definition: Hiding latency locally and correcting afterwards.
interop_reason: Latency hiding is local repair work, so its absence is felt as lag.

name: Transport protocol
definition: The wire protocol carrying session traffic.
interop_reason: With no shared wire protocol there is no session to join at all.

name: Media transport
definition: Carrying live audio and video streams.
interop_reason: Live audio and video degrade or drop out while the visit continues.

name: Session establishment
definition: Joining a running world, including authentication.
interop_reason: Joining a running world, authentication included, is the door: no agreement, no entry.

name: Session handoff and portals
definition: Leaving one world and arriving in another with state intact.
interop_reason: This row is the portal itself, and the travel use case is nothing but the handoff.

name: Presence and roster
definition: Knowing who is where, across operators.
interop_reason: A roster that does not cross operators means you cannot see who is where, but you can still be there.

name: World addressing and naming
definition: Naming a place and resolving that name to a reachable destination.
interop_reason: A destination name that does not resolve cannot be travelled to, so naming and resolution are the first agreement.

name: Discovery
definition: Finding worlds, nodes or services without knowing them in advance.
interop_reason: Worlds can be reached by a known address, so discovery adds reach rather than making it possible.

name: Clock and time model
definition: Shared time so events order consistently.
interop_reason: A shared clock keeps events in order; without one the ordering drifts and coarse clocks still hold the session together.

name: Identity root
definition: The base identifier for a person, agent or thing.
interop_reason: With no shared base identifier the same person or agent is a stranger in every world they enter.

name: Credential format
definition: How verifiable claims about a subject are expressed.
interop_reason: Claims about age, membership or ownership are worthless if the receiving world cannot read them.

name: Credential exchange protocol
definition: How two parties request and present credentials.
interop_reason: A credential nobody can ask for or present is not a credential, and one subject reaches this row natively today.

name: Capability and permission grant
definition: What a subject may do, readable by a party that did not issue it.
interop_reason: A world that cannot read what an arriving person or agent is allowed to do must either refuse it or trust it blindly.

name: Selective disclosure
definition: Revealing only what a receiving world needs.
interop_reason: Without selective disclosure the traveller over-shares, which is a harm rather than a stop.

name: Reputation and social graph
definition: Portable relationships and standing.
interop_reason: Relationships and standing that do not travel leave the person present but unknown.

name: Rights enforcement
definition: Acting on licence terms at the point of use.
interop_reason: The terms themselves must cross, and that row is a must; acting on them is the receiver's own behaviour, and no agreed mechanism exists yet.

name: Geospatial pose
definition: Position and orientation expressed against the Earth.
interop_reason: Content pinned to the Earth must land in the same place in the other system, and a pose that cannot be read puts it somewhere else.

name: Coordinate reference systems
definition: Agreeing which frame coordinates are expressed in.
interop_reason: A frame disagreement is measured in metres or kilometres, not in taste.

name: Local anchors
definition: Fixing content to a place on one device.
interop_reason: An anchor made on one device never leaves it; the sharing case is the next row.

name: Shared and persistent anchors
definition: Fixing content to a place across devices and sessions.
interop_reason: Two people in two systems must see the same thing in the same spot, and today one subject reaches this row, through an extension.

name: Visual positioning
definition: Recovering precise pose from camera imagery.
interop_reason: Recovering pose from imagery can fall back to satellite position and manual alignment, at worse accuracy.

name: Tiled terrain and city streaming
definition: Streaming large geospatial 3D data by tile.
interop_reason: City-scale data is streamed by tile, and a tileset the receiving client cannot stream has to be converted before it is usable.

name: Indoor mapping
definition: Structured description of interior spaces.
interop_reason: A structured description of an interior makes placement and routing better; without one both are cruder, and nothing reaches this row today.

name: Immersive session lifecycle
definition: Starting, running and ending an immersive session on a device.
interop_reason: The visitor's app and the device runtime are two independent systems, and if they cannot start an immersive session the visit does not happen.

name: Controller input
definition: Buttons, sticks and pose from handheld devices.
interop_reason: A world that reads controllers differently is harder to use, and pointer and text paths remain.

name: Hand tracking
definition: Articulated hand pose as an input source.
interop_reason: Hand tracking adds a way in, and its absence falls back to controllers.

name: Eye tracking
definition: Gaze direction as input, with its privacy constraints.
interop_reason: Gaze is an aid with privacy limits, and everything works without it.

name: Haptics
definition: Touch feedback to the user.
interop_reason: Touch feedback is felt when it is missing, and nothing stops.

name: Device capability discovery
definition: Learning what the client device can actually do.
interop_reason: A world that cannot ask what the arriving device can do will guess, and guessing wrong costs quality rather than entry.

name: Scripting runtime
definition: The language and runtime that expresses world rules.
interop_reason: The language a world writes its rules in is its own business and never has to cross.

name: Behaviour graphs and interactivity
definition: Declarative interactivity that travels with an asset.
interop_reason: The use case says the asset must behave, so a door that will not open in the second system is the failure this row names.

name: Sandboxing and isolation
definition: Running untrusted content safely, with limits.
interop_reason: A host can sandbox guest content on its own; agreement only makes the limits predictable for the guest.

name: Agent integration
definition: Autonomous agents acting inside a world.
interop_reason: An agent with no agreed way to perceive and act in a world it did not come from cannot join it at all.

name: Resource budgets
definition: Bounding memory, time and calls for guest content.
interop_reason: Without agreed limits, guest content and agents are throttled or refused unpredictably.

name: World state persistence
definition: What survives a restart of the world.
interop_reason: What survives a restart is mostly the host's business; it crosses the boundary only when a visitor's changes must last.

name: Inventory
definition: Items a user holds, and whether they travel.
interop_reason: The use case names inventory, and items that cannot be read at the destination do not travel with the person.

name: Preference portability
definition: Settings and accessibility choices that follow the user.
interop_reason: The use case names preferences, and for a person who depends on comfort and accessibility settings, arriving without them ends the visit.

name: Content addressing
definition: Referring to content by hash rather than location.
interop_reason: Naming content by hash makes an item the same item everywhere; without it copies drift while still loading.

name: Bundle format
definition: How a runnable experience is packaged.
interop_reason: A runnable experience moves between hosts far less often than an asset does, and repackaging is the fallback.

name: Content delivery
definition: Getting assets to clients at scale.
interop_reason: Assets reach clients over ordinary web delivery, so agreement here buys scale and cost rather than possibility.

name: Versioning and update
definition: Shipping changes without breaking existing content.
interop_reason: A reader that cannot tell which version it holds, or what to do with the parts it does not know, breaks on the first update, which is the "no hand fixes" test again.

name: Conformance testing
definition: Proving an implementation actually matches the specification.
interop_reason: Every other must row is a claim until a shared test says it holds, which is exactly what the meeting asked for.

name: World generation from a prompt or an image
definition: Producing a whole three-dimensional place from a description or a picture, rather than reconstructing one that exists — and whether what comes out is a scene a receiver can keep, or frames it can only watch.
interop_reason: A generated place that arrives only as frames to watch still reaches the viewer, but as a recording rather than a world the receiver can open and use.

name: Simulation from a learned model
definition: A model that continues a world in response to what the viewer does, producing each next moment itself instead of handing over a scene for an engine to run — with the stated limits on trusting that prediction.
interop_reason: A world continued by a model still reaches a viewer, but only as what the model chooses to show, so the receiver cannot keep it or run it again.

name: Photogrammetric object capture
definition: Building a textured three-dimensional model from a set of ordinary photographs of a real object.
interop_reason: How a system turns photographs into a model is its own method, and what leaves is an ordinary asset the container and geometry rows already carry.

name: Splat data interchange format
definition: Carrying Gaussian splat data between tools and runtimes as a named format, as distinct from being able to render splats already in memory.
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so this row is what geometry encoding is for a mesh: splat content in a named format the receiving tool cannot read does not arrive at all, and re-exporting it is the hand fix the use case forbids.

name: Captured-scene streaming
definition: Delivering a captured scene progressively, by region and by detail level, so a viewer starts before the whole scene has arrived and never holds more than it can draw.
interop_reason: Without an agreed order for what arrives first, a large capture still loads, it just makes the viewer wait for the whole of it.

name: Volumetric video capture and playback
definition: A captured, time-varying three-dimensional scene carried and replayed as media, rather than authored as geometry, including the camera calibration and mask metadata a second implementation would need to reproduce it.
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so a volumetric clip is an asset like any other: without the calibration and mask metadata a second implementation needs, what arrives is not the recording and no one can make it one by hand.

name: Point cloud encoding
definition: How a set of points, each with a position and zero or more attributes, is encoded and compressed.
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so a point cloud encoded in a way the receiver cannot decode is not a point cloud, exactly as an undecodable mesh is not a mesh, and that capture shows nothing.

name: Multi-view plus depth
definition: Carrying a scene as several calibrated camera views with per-pixel depth, together with the camera intrinsics and extrinsics needed to reproject them.
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so views that arrive without their intrinsics and extrinsics cannot be reprojected: the capture lands as loose pictures rather than as the place it recorded.

name: Novel view synthesis
definition: Producing an image from a viewing position that no capture camera occupied.
interop_reason: Making an image from a viewpoint no camera occupied is a method inside one system, and what crosses to a second system is the picture it produced.

name: Time-varying capture
definition: Carrying a captured scene that changes over time, so that a receiver can play it back at the right rate without being handed each frame as an unrelated file.
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so a moving capture handed over as unrelated frames is not the capture: the receiver has to guess the rate and the ordering the sender already knew, and guessing is the hand fix the use case forbids.

name: Relighting captured content
definition: Making a captured scene respond to the lighting of the place it is dropped into, rather than staying lit as it was on the day it was photographed.
interop_reason: Whether a captured scene answers the light around it is work the receiving system does, and the asset arrives either way.

name: Editing a capture after the fact
definition: Changing a captured scene — cropping, deleting, recolouring — in a way that survives export, and that applies consistently to every frame of a moving capture.
interop_reason: Editing a capture happens in the tool that holds it, and what leaves is the edited asset, which the format rows already carry.

name: Generative editing of a world
definition: Changing a world that has already been made by describing the change in words or pointing at a region, and growing it past its original edges, with earlier versions kept rather than overwritten.
interop_reason: Describing a change to a world you already made is one service's own interface, and the world that results still leaves by the ordinary export rows.

name: Control over what gets generated
definition: What a generating system accepts as a specification of the world it should make — a description, one or several reference images with their placement, a panorama, a video, a seed, or uploaded coarse geometry — and in which interchange formats that specification may arrive.
interop_reason: A generator that cannot read the specification another tool wrote still produces a world, it just will not be the world that was asked for.

name: Deriving conventional assets from a generated scene
definition: Turning a splat or radiance-field world into the representations a conventional engine already understands — a collision mesh, a mesh for drawing, a panorama, a video — and stating what is lost in each.
interop_reason: Derived meshes and panoramas are how a generated world reaches a conventional engine at all, and each route loses something the receiver has to be told about.

name: Action and control exchange
definition: Carrying an agent's actions — poses, joint or gripper values, camera motion — into and out of a system as time-sampled data, with the embodiment, the frame, the units and any normalisation stated, so a second implementation can read them.
interop_reason: Actions that arrive without their embodiment, frame and units cannot be replayed elsewhere, so an agent acts only in the system it was written for.

name: Panoramic scene imagery
definition: Carrying a full 360-degree view of a place as an image, with its projection stated, so a receiver can use it as a scene, as a backdrop, or as a light source.
interop_reason: A panorama whose projection is not stated is still an image, but the receiver has to guess before it can use it as a backdrop or as a light.

name: Real-world reconstruction
definition: Producing a geometric description of the space around a device from its own sensors — mesh, planes, or a parametric room — while the session runs, and whether that description can leave the session it was made in.
interop_reason: A reconstruction that cannot leave the device that made it keeps the room private to one session, so anything placed against it has to be fitted again elsewhere.

name: Semantic labelling of the real world
definition: Naming what a real surface, object or pixel is — floor, wall, sky, road, person — as per-pixel classes or detected objects, in a channel set an application can read by name, and carried so another system can act on it.
interop_reason: Labels each vendor names differently still serve one application, but a second one cannot act on floor or sky without being rewritten for that vendor.

name: Real-world depth
definition: Per-pixel distance from the camera to real surfaces, from a depth sensor or inferred from camera imagery, in metric units.
interop_reason: Depth reported in units the receiver does not share puts real surfaces at the wrong distance, so content is placed badly rather than not at all.

name: Real-world occlusion
definition: Hiding virtual content behind real surfaces, from live depth, a reconstructed mesh, or a blend of the two.
interop_reason: Whether real surfaces hide virtual content is drawn on the device that sees them, and none of that decision crosses to a second system.

name: Passthrough and environment blending
definition: Mixing the live camera view of the real world with rendered content, and controlling how much of each the viewer sees, including cutting a hole in a virtual environment to let a real object through.
interop_reason: How much of the real room a runtime lets through is its own presentation, and an arriving asset cannot tell the difference.

name: Face and body tracking as input
definition: The user's own facial expression and body pose delivered as a live sensor stream, with the privacy constraints that go with it — distinct from the format an avatar stores, which is avatar.expression.
interop_reason: A face and body stream in a shape the receiver does not read leaves the avatar still rather than absent, and its privacy terms have to be agreed with it.

name: Navigable space and arrival points
definition: Saying where in a place a body may stand, walk and arrive — walkable surface, bounds, spawn points — carried with the scene rather than recomputed by whoever opens it.
interop_reason: A place that arrives without its walkable surface and arrival points still loads, but whoever opens it has to work out where a body may stand and where a portal lands.

name: Permanent code identity
definition: Naming a published unit of logic so that the name resolves to the same thing forever, and so no second author can ever claim it.
interop_reason: A published unit of logic whose name resolves to something else elsewhere still runs, but nobody can be sure which code they called.

name: Content review and safety gating
definition: Review that stands between finished content and the people who will see it, and who performs it — including whether a receiving world can tell what review a piece of arriving content has already had.
interop_reason: A receiving world that cannot tell what review arriving content has already had still shows it, and has to repeat the whole review itself.

name: Map lifecycle and alignment
definition: Declaring that a map of a place exists, with its version and lifecycle, and publishing the transform that aligns it to another map of the same place.
interop_reason: Two maps of one place with no published transform between them put the same content in two positions, so a person arrives beside where they meant to be.

name: Coverage declaration
definition: Declaring the geographic area a service, dataset or piece of content applies to, in a stated frame, so a client can test whether it is relevant where the client is.
interop_reason: A service that never declares where it applies still answers, so a client has to call it and find out instead of testing whether it is relevant.

name: Extension mechanism
definition: A declared way to add data or behavior, with names and rules for recipients that do not implement the extension.
interop_reason: A receiver must distinguish required additions from optional ones or it cannot safely interpret an arriving asset or exchange.

name: Named subsets and levels
definition: Named subsets, components, or levels with stated requirements, allowing an implementation and content to declare a compatible contract.
interop_reason: Named subsets make compatible requirements easier to select, while systems can still agree on the individual requirements without a named profile.

name: Colour space and dynamic range
definition: Declaring the color interpretation and output range of images, textures, and rendering surfaces so receivers can perform the required conversions.
interop_reason: Content still arrives when color conventions differ, but its colors and brightness can change visibly.

name: Domain metadata carried with an asset
definition: Structured descriptive properties attached to a scene or its parts, with enough declared structure for another system to read them.
interop_reason: An asset can load without shared descriptive properties, but receivers lose the classifications and facts that drive its use.

name: Assurance and evidence behind a claim
definition: Evidence and assurance information accompanying a claim, enabling the relying party to assess how the claim was established.
interop_reason: A credential can be presented without shared assurance detail, but the receiver has less evidence for deciding whether to trust it.

name: Claim vocabulary and schema
definition: Declaring the vocabulary, types, and validation schemas needed to interpret and check the structure of a claim.
interop_reason: A receiving world cannot use a credential reliably unless it can interpret the claim vocabulary and check its structure.

name: Pairwise identifiers and unlinkability
definition: Pairwise identifiers and presentation mechanisms that reduce correlation across relationships, with their remaining correlation risks stated.
interop_reason: Travel can continue with reusable identifiers, but correlating visits across relationships creates a privacy loss.

name: Preview image for an asset
definition: A preview image referenced or packaged with an asset, usable without rendering its three-dimensional contents.
interop_reason: A moved asset remains usable without a shared preview image, but selection and arrival previews become slower or less informative.

name: Encryption keys and confidential delivery
definition: Identifying recipient key material and algorithms that permit confidential communication or encrypted content for an intended subject.
interop_reason: Travel and participation can use a shared session without encrypted subject payloads, but lack of agreement prevents confidential subject data from following safely.

name: Key rotation, revocation and recovery
definition: Rules for changing, revoking, or recovering identity-control keys and for discovering the applicable verification material.
interop_reason: After identity keys change, a destination must find the applicable verification material to recognize the same person or agent safely.

name: Credential status and revocation
definition: A defined mechanism to discover the suspension, revocation, or other status of a credential after issuance.
interop_reason: A destination cannot rely on an issued credential for admission or authority unless the agreed mechanism lets it discover that the credential has been withdrawn.

name: Two-dimensional interface surfaces
definition: Layout and presentation of two-dimensional interface regions, including their size, alignment, and relationship to a display or scene.
interop_reason: A scene or visit can continue when interface layouts differ, but carried controls and information may become hard to use.

name: Real-world lighting estimation
definition: Runtime estimates of environmental illumination made available to content for lighting or reflections.
interop_reason: Estimating illumination for the local view stays within the sensing and rendering system and requires no agreement between the independent worlds in the four use cases.

name: Marker and image tracking
definition: Detecting recognized physical markers or images and reporting their tracked pose relative to a runtime reference space.
interop_reason: Shared marker references improve physical alignment across systems, while a scene or visit can still proceed with another placement method.

name: Asset reference resolution
definition: Resolving scene resource identifiers against a context or resolver so the referenced resources can subsequently be accessed.
interop_reason: An asset with external resources cannot load intact if the receiver cannot resolve its resource references in the intended context.

name: Pose series and live pose streams
definition: Time-associated pose sequences or streams describing an object's changing location and orientation, with any interpolation rules declared separately.
interop_reason: Systems exchanging moving subjects must agree on the time and frame of each pose or the subject's movement cannot be reconstructed correctly.

name: Pointing and selection against content
definition: Picking scene content from pointing input and reporting the intersected object or geometry to the application.
interop_reason: Turning local pointing input into a scene hit stays inside the receiving application and does not require agreement between independent worlds.

name: Text entry
definition: Receiving character or string entry through a defined input interface, separate from interpreting physical controller actions.
interop_reason: Receiving text through a local input field or keyboard interface is a device-side interaction and need not be shared between worlds.

name: Compositor layers
definition: Submitting distinct shaped image layers to a display compositor with their placement and composition properties.
interop_reason: The choice of image layers sent to a device compositor is local presentation work and need not be shared across a world boundary.

name: Bounding volumes and spatial index
definition: Bounding volumes associated with scene content, organized for spatial rejection, traversal, or selection before detailed geometry is loaded.
interop_reason: Shared bounds let a receiver select content before loading its geometry; without them the content can still move but loads and traverses less efficiently.

name: Named sets of objects
definition: Named or rule-defined sets of scene objects that consumers can use as targets for scene operations.
interop_reason: Losing agreed object sets weakens grouped scene operations while the individual objects can still be transferred and rendered.

name: Transform constraints
definition: Authored runtime relationships that constrain one node's transform using another node and defined evaluation rules.
interop_reason: A moved object or avatar can still load when constraints are lost, but linked movement and pose behavior degrade.

name: Timed media inside a scene
definition: Referencing timed audiovisual media inside a scene and defining the synchronization needed to present it as scene content.
interop_reason: A scene can transfer without agreed media timing, but its video, sound and coordinated presentation can be lost or drift.

name: Usable physical area
definition: Runtime-reported physical play-area bounds and floor-relative reference information available to an application.
interop_reason: Physical play-area bounds and floor references describe one device's surroundings and can remain local while the four cross-system use cases proceed.

name: Sound generated at play time
definition: Generating audio during playback from an exchanged synthesis model, supporting data, and changing control parameters.
interop_reason: A moved scene remains usable without its agreed synthesis model, but generated sound and its response to changing controls are lost.

name: Content protection signalling
definition: Declaring the protection scheme associated with protected content components so recipients can identify the required protection mechanism.
interop_reason: A receiver cannot access protected transferred content unless it can identify the protection mechanism required for that content.

name: Linked pose structures
definition: Interchanging linked poses and transforms as chains or graphs so related frames can be reconstructed consistently.
interop_reason: Without agreed links and transform meaning, receivers cannot reconstruct the same related frames for transferred content or participants.

name: Published zones and spatial events
definition: Interchanging identified spatial zones, typed events scoped to them, and summaries with defined spatial and temporal meaning.
interop_reason: Travel and participation can continue without shared zone-event meaning, but spatial notifications and summaries lose useful context.

name: Consent carried with the subject
definition: Carrying a grant of permission with scope, purpose, validity, and withdrawal information for uses of the subject or represented data.
interop_reason: A recipient that cannot interpret the carried permission cannot determine whether the requested use of the subject or data is authorized.

name: Record of what a system decided
definition: A machine-readable account of a recipient's evaluation and action, with any signature or integrity proof explicitly identified.
interop_reason: A shared evaluation receipt makes cross-system actions auditable, while travel or participation can still occur without that record.

name: Deciding whether to admit an arrival
definition: A destination's pre-arrival approval or refusal response, including any validity limit and optional explanatory information.
interop_reason: A traveller or agent cannot safely complete entry unless the origin and destination understand the destination's approval, refusal and validity conditions.

name: General-purpose GPU computation
definition: Dispatching programmable non-raster GPU workloads against resources available through the graphics-compute API.
interop_reason: Choosing and dispatching internal GPU computation does not require agreement between the systems that exchange an asset.

name: Frame pacing and predicted display time
definition: Coordinating frame submission with predicted display timing and the view poses associated with that time.
interop_reason: Disagreement between an arriving application and the device runtime about display timing degrades the view through stale poses or poor frame pacing.

name: Portable shader language
definition: A specified shader source language and execution semantics enabling implementations to consume the same shader program.
interop_reason: An asset can still load with fallback materials when its shaders are not understood, but authored appearance degrades.

name: Exact and parametric geometry
definition: Carrying parametric curves and surfaces in mathematical form so a receiver can evaluate or tessellate them.
interop_reason: A receiver that cannot evaluate the transmitted curves and surfaces cannot reconstruct an asset whose geometry is carried in that form.

name: Emitter-based effects
definition: Exchanging particle-system emitters and simulation/rendering parameters that a receiving runtime evaluates.
interop_reason: Losing an exchanged emitter's parameters removes or changes visual effects while the containing asset or avatar can still arrive.

name: Recovering a stripped provenance record
definition: Locating associated provenance through a supported content fingerprint or watermark when embedded association has been lost.
interop_reason: A stripped provenance record weakens trust in an arriving asset while the asset remains usable.

name: Declarative styling carried apart from the content
definition: Separately expressed styling rules that select feature visibility, color, or other supported display properties from content metadata.
interop_reason: Without shared styling rules, a moved scene can still load while its metadata-driven visibility and appearance change.

name: Selectable variants of an asset
definition: Named alternatives of an asset's authored configuration, with a defined selection mechanism.
interop_reason: A default asset can arrive when variant selection is lost, but the chosen configuration of the asset or avatar changes.

name: Voxel volumes
definition: Interchanging spatial cell volumes and their properties, including updates, as a scene representation.
interop_reason: A receiver that cannot decode the exchanged cells and their properties cannot reconstruct content represented as a voxel volume.

name: Hit test against the real world
definition: Asking a sensing runtime for ray intersections with its estimate of physical surroundings and receiving hit poses.
interop_reason: A disagreement about sensing hit results makes placement and interaction worse, while manual placement can keep the experience usable.

name: Privacy terms on sensed data
definition: Sensed-data disclosure controls such as spatial coarsening, payload use/retention declarations, and restricted or pseudonymous pose publication.
interop_reason: Without shared sensed-data disclosure terms, content, avatars, travellers and agents can still operate but may expose more data than intended.

name: Musical event-device input
definition: Receiving typed musical instrument events with channel, note or control identifiers and values through a documented device or recorded-event input interface.
interop_reason: Without an agreed musical-event interface, an arriving performance or interactive experience loses instrument input while other interaction paths remain.

name: Radiance-field reconstruction
definition: Reconstructing a radiance field or Gaussian representation from observed images and camera information, including optimization controls and a trained scene usable for subsequent view synthesis.
interop_reason: The fitting method stays inside the capture tool, while the resulting field crosses through the separate representation and format capabilities.

name: Generation of individual 3D objects
definition: Producing an individual three-dimensional object from a text or image prompt, with geometry or another renderable representation available for placement in a separately authored scene.
interop_reason: The generation method stays inside one tool, while its placeable output travels through the ordinary asset and representation capabilities.

name: Experience containment
definition: Whether a runtime can host another party's experience as a running thing, with its own logic and lifecycle, inside a containing world.
interop_reason: If two systems disagree on what a contained experience may do, the containment either fails or becomes a security hole; there is no partial agreement that works.

name: Unattended world coupling
definition: Whether state in one world can cause change in another with no participant present in either.
interop_reason: A coupling that carries change without anyone crossing needs both ends to agree on authority, ordering and settlement, or the two worlds silently diverge.

name: Machine and agent payments
definition: A defined exchange in which a person or an agent receives payment requirements, authorizes a payment and obtains a settlement result for a resource or service, with the scheme, network and asset named.
interop_reason: The agent use case says an agent pays for what it uses; if payer and payee share no payment exchange, the payment cannot happen at all.

name: Entitlements and licence checks at use
definition: Checking, at the moment of use, whether an identified holder has a current grant to enter, load, use or carry a resource, with the binding of holder to resource, expiry, revocation and transfer rules.
interop_reason: A destination that cannot read a grant must refuse the item, the entry or the agent, or admit it blindly.

name: Receipts and proofs of purchase
definition: A portable, machine-readable record of a purchase or grant that binds recipient, resource, issuer, time and the supporting transaction or grant evidence, and states which fields are signed so another verifier can check it.
interop_reason: A grant can still be checked with its issuer without a portable receipt, but a third system cannot verify the purchase on its own.

name: Governed trust registries
definition: Discovering and applying governed configuration that says which issuers, services or worlds a verifier should accept, with its governing authority, the meaning of an entry, update, removal and delegation rules, and the time or version that applies.
interop_reason: Credentials still verify without a shared registry, but each receiver must decide alone whom to trust, so acceptance differs from world to world.

name: Agent authoring and publishing interface
definition: A documented interface through which an AI agent or other program, working from outside a world or platform, can create, change and publish its content, such as an MCP server, a REST interface, a command line or a published instruction file, with the scope of what the agent may change stated.
interop_reason: An agent can still build in each platform through that platform's own interface, but without a shared one every agent needs a separate integration for every platform.

name: Taking a whole world out
definition: Exporting and importing a whole place, with its scenes, assets, behaviour and settings, in open and documented files, and stating what survives and where it can go if the host closes.
interop_reason: Assets can still move one at a time, but a place that cannot leave its host as a whole has to be rebuilt by hand when the host changes or closes.

name: Model-based object tracking
definition: Recognising a known physical object from its 3D model, without markers or prepared images, and reporting its pose so content stays registered to it.
interop_reason: The object model arrives from another system, so its format and units must be readable by the tracker, while the tracking itself stays on the device.

name: Remote (split) rendering
definition: Rendering a view on a server from the client's predicted pose and streaming the frames back for display, so a device shows content it could not draw itself.
interop_reason: Recorded descriptively by the owner's decision of 2026-09-18: the Atlas records which systems render remotely and does not define an agreement between client and renderer.

name: Live data binding
definition: Binding objects in a world to an external live data source, such as a sensor, machine controller or building system, so their state follows the real asset, or the real controller drives the simulated one.
interop_reason: A digital twin can still be shown without a shared binding, but each data source must be wired by hand; the Atlas's four use cases do not yet include digital twins, so the row is recorded against content that moves.

name: Activity and learning records
definition: A portable statement of what a person did in a world and with what result, readable by a system outside it, such as a learning record store, an employer or an assessor.
interop_reason: Training still finishes without a portable record, but the result stays in one vendor's dashboard instead of travelling with the person.

name: Physiological signals as input
definition: Heart rate, skin conductance and similar body signals delivered to an application as a live stream, with the privacy constraints that go with them.
interop_reason: Sensors and experiences come from different vendors; without a shared signal description each adaptation is wired to one device, though the experience still runs without it.
